items.title: Enter does not submit the profile dialogs, so the fastest path through them is mouse-only
items.summary: Confirmed and fixed at the cause. Both profile dialogs are a single auto-focused, pre-filled TextField with no onSubmitted, so the focused field swallowed Return and the only way to commit was to leave the keyboard. Added textInputAction: TextInputAction.done + onSubmitted: (_) => _submit() to the Create dialog's name field (screen_shell.dart:777) and the Duplicate dialog's name field (screen_shell.dart:905). _submit is the same method the primary button calls, so nothing is bypassed: an empty/whitespace name is still refused with the inline error, and a duplicate name that collides with an existing profile is still rejected. The Create dialog's description field is deliberately untouched — it is maxLines: 2, where Return is a newline.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/equipment_profile_dialog_submit_test.dart — three cases driven by tester.testTextInput.receiveAction(TextInputAction.done) (what a hardware Return reaches the focused field as), never by tapping the action button: Duplicate creates the copy and closes, Create creates the profile and closes, and an all-whitespace name is refused with 'Enter a profile name.'
items.revert_check: Removed both `onSubmitted: (_) => _submit(),` lines (screen_shell.dart:777 and :905): 3 of 3 tests fail (Return does nothing, the dialog stays up, the notifier is never called). Restored: 3/3 pass, and the pre-existing equipment_profile_duplicate_name_test.dart / equipment_profile_import_authority_test.dart still pass.

items.title: Import failures are reported as raw Dart exception text ('Import failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 1)')
items.summary: Confirmed; the finding's file was wrong (the import handler is screen_shell.dart's _importProfiles, not profile_controls.dart, which contains only presentational widgets). Fixed both halves the finding names. (1) Exports now identify themselves: exportProfileToJson and exportAllProfilesToJson both write profileExportEnvelope() = {format: 'skotiq.equipment-profile', version: 2, exportDate, profiles: [...]}, so the importer has something to check against. (2) profilesFromExportDocument() accepts every shape already on disk (the new envelope, the pre-envelope {version, profiles} batch, a bare single-profile map, a bare list) and rejects everything else in operator prose, never a Dart toString: a non-JSON file is told it 'is not a Skotiq equipment profile — it is not JSON at all', unrelated JSON that it 'contains no profile data', another product's export is named back, and a document whose format version is newer than this build gets 'exported by a newer version of Skotiq ... Update Skotiq and import it again' instead of being half-parsed into a wrong profile. (3) parseExportedProfile() restates each field-level rejection naming the profile ('Skotiq could not import "Widefield": focalLength must be non-negative.') or its position. (4) The screen substitutes the picked file's name (describeProfileImportFailure), so the message names the file the operator chose.
items.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/profile_export_format_test.dart — 11 cases: the envelope carries format+version and round-trips; each rejection message is asserted to contain the operator wording and NOT to contain 'FormatException' or a character offset; and the three legacy document shapes still import (backwards compatibility, since those files are on people's disks).
items.revert_check: Replaced the guarded decode in profilesFromExportDocument with the old bare `data = jsonDecode(json);` (profile_export_data.dart:55): 'a non-JSON file says so instead of naming a character offset' fails with the raw FormatException. Restored: 11/11 pass; full skotiq_core test/services suite green (2683 tests).

items.title: About shows 6.1.0 but drops the build number, and System Information omits everything a support ticket needs
items.summary: Half was already closed by an earlier wave, verified in the tree rather than assumed: about_settings.dart already renders 'Version ${version} (build ${buildNumber})'. The System Information half was real — Platform / OS Version / Dart Version and nothing else, none of which distinguishes two installs of the same release, and no way to hand any of it to a bug report except by retyping. The card now renders systemInformationProvider: Skotiq version+build, Platform, OS version, Dart, 'Connected to' (this computer, or the named imaging host — a remote client's facts were otherwise indistinguishable from a local one's), the database schema version, and the resolved data folder; plus a Copy button that puts the block on the clipboard as 'label: value' lines. The data folder is a separate FutureProvider on purpose: path_provider is a platform channel, and awaiting it inside the main provider put the whole card behind a spinner — which hung every pre-existing About test's pumpAndSettle until I split it. I did not add the Rust bridge version: nothing in the Dart layer exposes one today, and inventing a number for a support ticket is worse than omitting it.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/about_system_information_test.dart — the rendered block names the build, the schema and the data folder; Copy is asserted through a mocked Clipboard.setData platform channel to contain all three; and the default (un-overridden) collector is asserted to report '6.1.0 (build 25)' plus a 'Connected to' fact.
items.revert_check: Changed the collector's first fact back to `SupportFact('Skotiq', version.version)` (about_settings.dart:238, dropping the build number): 'the default collector reports the build number and the host' fails. Restored: 3/3 pass, and all 18 About tests (links, license, update-check, system-information) pass together.

items.title: Replay & Debug is written for the developer who built it: a lowercase title sentence and two user-facing dialogs that name a database table
items.summary: Confirmed on all four counts. (1) The page header is now 'Replay & Debug' — matching the settings entry that navigates to it, which already read 'Replay & Debug' — with a sentence-cased description of what the retention window is for, replacing 'decision-log retention + cleanup for the retrospective Replay screen.'. (2) 'persisted to the sequence_decisions table' and 'This deletes every row in the sequence_decisions table' are gone; no user-facing string in the page names a SQL table. (3) The confirmation states the magnitude before asking for consent: 'This deletes all 3 recorded decisions, for every past run.' That needed a real count, so ReplayDebugService.countAll() was added, GET /api/sequencer/replay-debug/decisions/count now counts every row when runId is omitted (existing per-run callers are unaffected), NetworkBackend.replayCountAllDecisions() reads it, and ReplayDebugSettingsController.countAllHistory() returns null when the authority cannot say — an older host answers 400 — in which case the dialog says 'every decision Skotiq has recorded' rather than inventing a number. (4) The dialog is now the shared ConfirmDialog with isDestructive: true, so 'Clear history' is the filled destructive button and Cancel is a ghost, matching the profile-delete dialog.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/replay_debug_clear_confirmation_test.dart — the confirmation contains 'all 3 recorded decisions' and never 'sequence_decisions'; the confirm button's variant is ButtonVariant.destructive while Cancel's is not; a null count renders the no-number wording with no fabricated quantity. apps/desktop/test/headless_api/replay_debug_handlers_test.dart asserts the count endpoint answers with every row when runId is omitted. The two pre-existing authority tests (host switch mid-confirmation, late result from the old host) were updated to the new labels and still pass.
items.revert_check: (a) Replaced `final total = await c.countAllHistory();` with `final int? total = null;` (replay_debug_settings.dart:242): 'the confirmation states how many decisions it will delete' fails. (b) Removed the `if (!params.containsKey('runId'))` branch (replay_debug_handlers.dart:61): the desktop handler test fails on the unfiltered count. Both restored: 3/3 + 4/4 pass. settings_search_index.g.dart regenerated so the search gate stays green.

items.title: Seven paired devices are all called 'Android companion' with no way to tell them apart before revoking
items.summary: Fixed the part that is objectively wrong rather than a matter of taste: the host has always stored what each token is allowed to do (paired_devices.auth_grant_spec, default 'control', 'admin' for a device that asked for it) and the list never showed it, so the row holding admin looked identical to a view-only one — at exactly the moment you are deciding what to revoke. Each row now carries an access badge beside the device-type label: 'Full access' (admin, warning-coloured), 'Can control the rig', 'View only', or 'Custom access' for the fine-grained `resource:level,...` form, with the raw spec on the tooltip. No new data is collected and no wire format changed; the value was already in the model the screen renders. The rest of the finding (rename, last-seen IP, real device model) is a product decision and is reported separately below, not implemented.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/pairing_access_badge_test.dart — three devices with the same name 'Android companion' and grants admin / view / fine-grained; the test asserts the three rows are word-for-word identical apart from exactly one 'Full access', one 'View only' and one 'Custom access' badge.
items.revert_check: Removed the `_AccessBadge(grantSpec: device.authGrantSpec)` line (pairing_screen.dart:711): the test fails. Restored: it passes, and the pre-existing pairing_screen_test.dart + pairing_completion_test.dart (8 tests) stay green.

items.title: Paired devices cannot be renamed, and nothing records which device on the network a row is
items.summary: Revisited and built option (b), the rename, which this entry had itself recommended; options (a) client-reported model and (c) last-client-IP remain genuinely open and are recorded below. On reflection the rename is not a matter of taste: paired_devices_table.dart:8 documents device_name as 'Device name provided during pairing (e.g. "John's iPhone")', but the only client that ever writes it sends a per-platform constant (apps/mobile/lib/services/mobile_pairing_service.dart:49-57 -> 'Android companion' for every Android device, forever), so the schema's own stated intent is unreachable by any operator action and revoking the handset you sold stays guesswork no matter how carefully you read the rows. Added PairingDatabase.renamePairedDevice (returns rows changed so a caller can tell a rename that hit nothing from one that landed), TokenManager.renameDevice (session token, grant and expiry untouched, so naming a device never disturbs one that is mid-run), PairingNotifier.renameDevice (same _enqueue/generation/backend-authority discipline as revoke and delete; refuses an empty name; on a row that has since been deleted it refreshes the list and reports failure rather than claiming a rename), and a 'Rename Device' row-menu action opening a one-field dialog that opens focused on the current name, commits on Return, and disables Save while the field is blank. Nothing new is collected, no wire format changed, and the write is to the same host database the list already reads.
items.options: Still open, and NOT implemented: (a) have the client report its real model — needs a device_info_plus dependency in apps/mobile and means the phone tells the host its make/model; rows become self-explanatory with no operator effort, but it adds a plugin and a privacy surface and does nothing for browsers. (c) record and show the last client IP — a new column written on token verification; identifies a device on the LAN with no client change, but starts retaining network data the app does not keep today, and DHCP makes it stale.
items.recommendation: (a) later if the owner is comfortable with the dependency — it would make new pairings self-labelling on top of the rename. (c) I would still not do: a stale IP is another confident-and-wrong statement of the kind this campaign keeps finding.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/pairing_rename_device_test.dart — 2 cases, both passing. Drives the REAL PairingNotifier against a real in-memory PairingDatabase holding two byte-identical 'Android companion' rows, opens the row menu, renames the first with Return, then asserts the dialog closed, the list shows one "Sean's Pixel" and one 'Android companion', the STORED row changed (database.getPairedDevice('phone-one').deviceName), that row's sessionToken and authGrantSpec are untouched, and the second device is unchanged. Second case types whitespace and asserts the dialog stays open and the stored name is unchanged. Existing pairing suites re-run together (access badge / screen / completion / rename): 10/10 pass; skotiq_remote_protocol full suite 207/207; translation_completeness_test.dart green for the two new en+es keys.
items.revert_check: Two probes. (1) Persistence severed: token_manager.dart renameDevice body replaced with `return true;` (repaint only, never reaches the row) — 'a paired device can be renamed, and the new name persists' FAILED at pairing_rename_device_test.dart:73, both rows still reading 'Android companion'. (2) Affordance severed: deleted the `value: 'rename'` PopupMenuItem from pairing_screen.dart — BOTH cases failed with no 'Rename Device' to tap. Both files restored from byte-copies (cmp reports IDENTICAL) and re-run: 2/2 pass; dart analyze clean on all four changed files.
items.caveats: The rename is host-side only: a phone that re-pairs still announces itself as 'Android companion', so a re-paired device returns to the generic name until it is renamed again. That is what option (a) would close.

items.title: 'Restore' asks you to restart the app afterwards but does not offer to, and nothing on the screen stays to remind you
items.summary: Confirmed and fixed at the cause: a permanent condition was being announced in a transient message. Both restore paths (a listed backup, and an imported file) now set a persistent banner on the Backup & Restore screen — 'Restart required' plus 'Restored N items. Restart Skotiq before the next run — until then this app is showing the state it had before the restore.' (or the imaging-host wording in remote mode) — which stays until the operator presses Dismiss. The snackbar is gone, so there is one message, not two. I did not add a 'Restart now' button: relaunching a Flutter desktop process from inside itself means spawning the executable and exiting, which is a real risk to take on a machine that may have a rig connected, and it is not needed to close the defect (the operator now cannot lose the message).
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/backup_restore_notice_test.dart — drives a real restore through the row action and the confirmation, asserts the banner appears, is STILL there after pumping 30 seconds (well past any snackbar's life), and disappears only on Dismiss. The pre-existing backup_import_authority_test.dart assertion on the old snackbar text was updated to the banner.
items.revert_check: Removed the `if (_restoreNotice != null) ... _RestoreNoticeBanner(...)` block from the screen body (backup_screen.dart:487): the new test fails. Restored: 6/6 backup tests pass.

items.title: A 426 MB abandoned GLADE download sat in the catalog directory for six weeks with nothing in the UI acknowledging it
items.summary: Confirmed as a real leak, with a narrower cause than the finding assumed. The download path already deletes its own `.partial` in a `finally` on both cancel and error (annotation_catalog_io.dart, legacy_catalog_io.dart), so a normal failure cleans up; what nothing handles is a process that dies mid-download — a crash, a kill, or a power cut — which is exactly how a 407 MiB leftover survives six weeks. Fixed at the cause: CatalogManager.initialize() now sweeps `*.partial` files in the catalog directory and logs the bytes reclaimed. That is safe and complete rather than cosmetic, because a partial is never resumable (each attempt opens the temp path with openWrite, which truncates), so there is nothing to offer to resume and nothing lost by deleting it; and the sweep runs at startup, before any download this process starts, so it cannot race one. I deliberately did NOT add a 'Partial download: 407 MB — Resume / Discard' card as the finding suggested: 'Resume' would be a lie about a file that is always thrown away, and 'Discard' is a button for a condition the app can simply not leave behind.
items.test: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/catalog_partial_sweep_test.dart — initialize() removes a 4 KiB glade_plus_galaxies.csv.partial while leaving an installed hygdata_v41.csv alone, and a directory with no leftovers is left with exactly its one file (the sweep touches only .partial).
items.revert_check: Removed the `await _sweepAbandonedPartials(dir);` call from initialize() (manager.dart:94): 'initialize reclaims an abandoned partial download' fails. Restored: 2/2 pass, and the whole skotiq_planetarium suite (494 tests) is green.

items.title: The Deep-Star Tier card tells an astrophotographer to build and host their own tileset with a repo tool
items.summary: Real, and the honesty half is already closed — deep_star_catalog_card.dart now reads 'No tileset is published yet: host one built with tools/catalog_prep and point the URL below at it', and the empty-URL note repeats it, so the card no longer implies a tileset exists. What is left is not a wording bug: a consumer settings page is offering a feature that no customer can use, and only the owner can decide whether that feature exists. I did not touch it, because every wording change without a hosting decision is cosmetic — exactly the disclosure-only 'fix' this campaign keeps catching.
items.options: (a) Publish an official tileset (the project already ships catalogs via a GitHub release — 'catalogs-v1' — so the machinery exists) and reduce the card to one toggle: the only version in which the deep-star tier is a real feature for a real customer, at the cost of building, hosting and versioning a large Gaia/Tycho-2 artifact. (b) Keep self-hosting as the only path but move the card behind an 'Advanced' disclosure and point at tools/catalog_prep/README.md (which exists) instead of a bare source path: zero infrastructure, ships today, but the feature stays developer-only and still occupies space in a shipping settings page. (c) Hide the tier from release builds until a tileset exists.
items.recommendation: (a) if the deep-star tier is meant to be a selling point — the bundled HYG floor is visible at imaging fields of view, which is where this tier matters — otherwise (b) as the honest interim, since it can ship immediately and stops the page reading like a developer's TODO. I would not pick (c): the code is built and works, and hiding it loses the ability for advanced users to use what is already there.
